extracted.intended_audience: attachers, utilities, broadband providers, and their counsel and other stakeholders participating in FCC pole-attachment proceedings and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules, disclosure requirements, and dispute-resolution criteria governing pole attachment applications, information requests, RBAT review, ex parte filings, comment procedures, and related regulatory compliance under FCC Part 1. Intended to guide parties (attachers, utilities, staff) in interactions and filings in pole-attachment disputes and broadband-deployment matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility notice and alternative qualified-contractor identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility must provide notice of this objection to the attacher and must identify at least one available qualified contractor that the attacher can use instead to perform simple surveys and make-ready work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a utility disqualifies an attacher’s chosen contractor for surveys/simple make-ready work, the utility is required to designate an available qualified contractor. The rule contemplates workforce constraints may affect availability and asks whether utilities are disqualifying otherwise-qualified outside contractors; where no qualified contractors exist, the Commission may consider remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis requirement (FRFA/IRFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Regulatory Flexibility Act, the agency must prepare a Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA) unless it certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; an Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) is prepared for the Further Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRFA is set forth in Appendix C and the IRFA in Appendix D. The Commission requests written public comments on the IRFA; such comments must be filed by the deadlines on the document’s first page and must have a separate and distinct heading designating them as responses to the IRFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) and OMB review for new/modified information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed new or modified information collection requirements in this document are subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act and must be submitted to OMB for review under Section 3507(d) of the PRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB, the public, and other federal agencies will be invited to comment on new/modified information collection requirements. Sections (e.g., amendments to 47 CFR §§ 1.1411, 1.1415, 1.1416) that may contain PRA-covered collections will be submitted to OMB and will not become effective until OMB review is complete. The Commission also seeks comment on reducing information-collection burdens on small businesses under the Small Business Paperwork Relief Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will send a copy of this Fourth Report and Order to Congress and the Government Accountability Office pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 801(a)(1)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard CRA submission procedure; included here as a required post-adoption transmission to Congress/GAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte presentation filing and content requirements (permit-but-disclose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proceeding is treated as a 'permit-but-disclose' proceeding. Persons making ex parte presentations must file a copy of any written presentation or a memorandum summarizing any oral presentation within two business days after the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoranda summarizing oral presentations must (1) list all persons attending/participating in the meeting, and (2) summarize all data presented and arguments made. If the presentation repeats data/arguments already in prior filings, the presenter may cite those filings (with page/paragraph references) instead of summarizing. Documents shown or given to staff during ex parte meetings are deemed written ex parte presentations and must be filed consistent with rule 1.1206(b). In proceedings governed by §1.49(f) or where the Commission provides electronic filing, written ex parte presentations, memoranda, and attachments must be filed through ECFS and in their native format (e.g., .doc, .xml, .ppt, searchable .pdf). Participants should familiarize themselves with the Commission’s ex parte rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period and filing procedures (ECFS and paper; no hand delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may file comments and reply comments pursuant to 47 CFR §§ 1.415 and 1.419 by the dates on the first page. Comments may be filed electronically via ECFS or by paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should refer to the docket number (e.g., WC Docket No. 17-84). Electronic filers use https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs. Paper filers must file an original and one copy and may use commercial overnight courier or U.S. Postal Service; effective March 19, 2020 the Commission no longer accepts hand or messenger delivered filings. Addresses: commercial overnight (except USPS Express/Priority) — 9050 Junction Drive, Annapolis Junction, MD 20701; USPS first-class/Express/Priority — 45 L Street NE, Washington, D.C. 20554.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act requirement (plain-language summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act requires agencies to post online a brief plain-language summary of proposed rules when providing notice of a rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will publish the required plain-language summary of this Further Notice on https://www.fcc.gov/proposed-rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible formats request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to request materials in accessible formats for people with disabilities (Braille, large print, electronic files, audio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be sent to fcc504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Governmental Affairs Bureau at 202-418-0530 (voice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule for adopted order and OMB-tied delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fourth Report and Order generally becomes effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, except amendments that may contain new/modified information-collection requirements will not become effective until OMB completes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to §1.1411(c)(4) and new §1.1415 (which may contain PRA obligations) will not become effective until OMB review is complete; the Wireline Competition Bureau will announce the effective date for those sections by subsequent Public Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: §1.1411(c)(4) — Request for information from cyclical pole inspection reports (timeliness and retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submitting its attachment application, a new attacher may request in writing that the utility provide, as to the poles covered by the attachment application, the information regarding those poles contained in the utility’s most recent cyclical pole inspection reports (or more recent inspection report). The utility shall provide this information within ten (10) business days of the new attacher’s written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities must retain copies of their pole inspection reports, in the form they are created, until a superseding report covering those poles is completed. A 'cyclical pole inspection report' is any report created in the normal course of business that sets forth routine inspection results during a utility’s normal pole inspection cycle. After requesting and receiving pole inspection information, a new attacher may amend an attachment application at any time until the utility grants or denies the original application. If a utility receives an amended application, it may, at its option, restart the 45-day (or 60-day for larger orders) period for responding and conducting a survey; if electing to restart, the utility must notify the attacher of that intent within five business days of receipt of the amended application or by the 45th (or 60th) day after the original application was considered complete, whichever is earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT establishment and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter-Bureau Rapid Broadband Assessment Team (RBAT) shall be established to prioritize and expedite resolution of pole attachment disputes alleged to impede or delay broadband deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RBAT shall consist of one or more staff from the Enforcement Bureau and one or more staff from the Wireline Competition Bureau, designated by senior staff in those Bureaus.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT roles, discretion, and recommended processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The RBAT shall prioritize resolution of alleged disputes impeding or delaying active broadband deployments, gather and promptly review pertinent information, and have discretion to decide the most appropriate process for resolving the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available processes include recommending RBAT-supervised mediation under §1.737, use of the Accelerated Docket, and other appropriate actions. RBAT-supervised mediation is generally voluntary, but the RBAT may require parties to participate in pre-filing settlement negotiations or mediation as a condition for Accelerated Docket inclusion. The RBAT may recommend Accelerated Docket placement based on the totality of enumerated factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to request RBAT review (FCC-5653 form requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing a formal complaint, a party may request RBAT review and assessment of a dispute that it believes is impeding or delaying broadband deployment by first notifying the Chief of the Enforcement Bureau’s Market Disputes Resolution Division (MDRD) by phone and in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MDRD Chief will direct the requesting party to form FCC-5653, Request for RBAT Review and Assessment, and to instructions for completing and electronically transmitting the form to the RBAT.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT meeting scheduling and information requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a completed Request for RBAT Review and Assessment, the RBAT shall schedule a meeting with all parties as soon as practicable and may request written responses or documentation from the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the initial meeting or shortly thereafter, RBAT will provide guidance on effective dispute-resolution means (RBAT-supervised mediation, Accelerated Docket, or other actions). If parties seek RBAT-supervised mediation, the MDRD Chief in consultation with RBAT may waive §1.737 procedures as appropriate given facts/circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 1 — Jurisdictional claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the prospective complainant states a claim for violation of the Act, or a Commission rule or order that falls within the Commission’s jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of multiple factors RBAT will consider (RBAT bases acceptance decision on the totality of listed factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 2 — Likely advancement of broadband deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether expedited resolution of a particular dispute or category of disputes appears likely to advance the deployment of broadband facilities or services, especially in an unserved or underserved area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in RBAT’s totality analysis for Accelerated Docket suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 3 — Exhaustion of settlement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the parties to the dispute have exhausted all reasonable opportunities for settlement during any staff-supervised mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether further staff-supervised settlement efforts have been tried before accelerating adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 4 — Number and complexity of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The number and complexity of the issues in dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer and less complex issues favor acceleration; complexity may counsel against Accelerated Docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 5 — Novelty of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the dispute raises new or novel issues versus settled interpretations of rules or policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel legal or factual questions may affect suitability for accelerated handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 6 — Likely need for and complexity of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The likely need for, and complexity of, discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant or complex discovery needs may weigh against accelerated resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 7 — Likely need for expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The likely need for expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters requiring substantial expert testimony may be less suitable for the Accelerated Docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 8 — Ability to stipulate to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of the parties to stipulate to facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater ability to stipulate to facts supports acceleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 9 — Existence of assembled evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the parties have already assembled relevant evidence bearing on the disputed facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases with assembled evidence are more amenable to expedited resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 10 — Willingness to seek rulings on subsets/test cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness of the prospective complainant to seek a ruling on a subset of claims or issues (e.g., threshold or 'test cases').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering a narrowed test case can support inclusion on the Accelerated Docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: RBAT factor 11 — Additional RBAT-discretion factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Such other factors as the RBAT, within its discretion, may deem appropriate and conducive to the prompt and fair adjudication of the complaint proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for RBAT’s case-specific discretionary considerations; RBAT evaluates all factors in totality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B proposed rule — 90-day extension for very large attachment requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility may add 90 days to the make-ready periods described in §1.1411(e) for all requests for attachment larger than the lesser of 3,000 poles or 5 percent of the utility’s poles in a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed revision to §1.1411(g)(4) specifying an allowable extension for very large orders; applies to compliance with time periods in §1.1411.
